title: Log Band Layout Explorer
description: The display groups the 256 FFT bins into a few bands. Because the ear judges pitch by ratio, the bands are log-spaced: each band's top edge is a fixed multiple of its bottom edge. For 16 bands from 100 Hz to 6,400 Hz that ratio is 64^(1/16) = 1.2968. The edges are rounded to whole bins, and a band narrower than one bin is stretched to one bin.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy

learningObjectives: The learner will use the 16-band log-spaced layout from 100 Hz to 6,400 Hz to find the band that contains 3 tones and the number of bins in 3 bands, with at least 5 of 6 correct.
prerequisites: frequency bin, bin width, band energy, log-spaced bands (all defined in this chapter above the block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Why does every band have a different number of bins?
Would equal-width bands put 1,000 Hz in the same band number as log bands?
Why do the bands start at 100 Hz instead of 0 Hz?
commonMisconceptions: (1) Every band has the same number of bins. (2) Equal-width bands and log-spaced bands put 1,000 Hz in the same band. (3) The highest band is the narrowest.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six challenges. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
